items.title: Trivial-potential classical charged-scalar Einstein–Maxwell system
items.design_state: Definition and global real-potential system, smooth well-definedness, tensor types and SI dimensions authored. The actual batch-4 scalar functional and batch-6 electrovacuum convention suppliers remain unaccepted drafts.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with its metric-selected Levi–Civita connection and independent orientation as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and the curvature and Hodge conventions of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]] and [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Fix $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and put $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$.

The **trivial-potential sector** consists of a global smooth real one-form $A\in\Omega^1(M)$ and a global smooth complex scalar field $\varphi\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)$. It defines the exact real two-form $F:=dA$ and the charged derivative

$$\pi_a:=(D\varphi)_a:=\nabla_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi,$$

where $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is an arbitrary fixed coupling. Define $D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$, with the conjugate derivative using $+i\lambda A_a$, and $D_a\pi^a:=g^{ab}D_a\pi_b$. Let $\mathcal U\subset\mathbb R$ be open with $|\varphi|^2(M)\subset\mathcal U$, let $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U;\mathbb R)$, and fix $K_\varphi>0$. Define

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{\pi_a}\pi_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad S_\varphi:=-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M L_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where on a noncompact $M$ the integral is used when finite and otherwise only compactly supported action differences are used. The scalar equation, current vector, and scalar stress tensor are

$$D_a\pi^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi\pi^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\pi_a}\pi_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi.$$

Put

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T_{ab}:=T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}.$$

The associated **classical charged-scalar Einstein–Maxwell system** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad D_a\pi^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0.$$

Here $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$; all indices are raised with $g^{-1}$. This is a definition of a mathematical system, not an adopted physical postulate or a claim about nature. It is restricted to a trivial real-potential sector: $F$ is exact, no nontrivial $U(1)$ bundle is included, and $\lambda$ is not quantized. The scalar is classical, and neither $K_\varphi$ nor $\lambda$ is tied to a Planck constant.

For formal SI bookkeeping in length coordinates, assign $[g_{ab}]=1$, $[x^a]=\mathrm m$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $[\varphi]=1$, $[\lambda]=\mathrm{Wb^{-1}}$, $[\pi_a]=\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, $[V]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and $[K_\varphi]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$. These give $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\kappa T_{ab}]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and $[S_\varphi]=\mathrm{J\,s}$. They are dimensions, not measured values.

items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented four-manifold without boundary. Its smooth
structure is retained throughout. A **classical finite-regularity
trivial-potential configuration** consists of a time-oriented $C^3$
Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a global real $C^2$ one-form
$A$, and a global complex $C^2$ scalar $\varphi$. Fix
$c,G_N,\mu_0,K_\varphi>0$, $\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and
$V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U;\mathbb R)$ for an open
$\mathcal U\subset\mathbb R$ containing $|\varphi|^2(M)$. Set
$\kappa_E=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The curvature sign, length-coordinate convention
$x^0=ct$, and SI assignments are those of
[[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]]; only these formulas and
conventions are imported, not that item's smooth-field restriction.

The Levi-Civita connection and curvature here are defined by their coordinate
formulas for this $C^3$ metric. Define

$$F_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,\qquad P_a:=\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi,$$

$$\mathcal D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b,\qquad E_\varphi:=g^{ab}\mathcal D_aP_b-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,$$

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi,\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

Conjugate charged derivatives use the opposite gauge sign. All indices are
raised with $g^{-1}$. Thus $F,P$ are $C^1$, $j,T^\varphi,T^{\mathrm{EM}}$
are $C^1$, $E_\varphi$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}$ are continuous, and the
Einstein tensor $G$ is $C^1$. The **classical charged-scalar equations** are
the pointwise equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad E_\varphi=0,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}).$$

Here $dF=0$ already follows from $F=dA$ with $A\in C^2$. These are equations
for the declared classical fields; they do not assert existence, smoothness
improvement, or a weaker distributional theory.

For a continuous compactly supported real top form $\omega$, define
$\mathcal I_M(\omega)$ by a finite smooth cutoff localization near its
support and the signed Riemann integrals of the resulting chart
coefficients, extended by zero. The construction and its independence are
proved below. For a complex top form extend $\mathcal I_M$ by integrating
its real and imaginary parts separately. For a configuration
$X=(g,A,\varphi)$ put

$$\mathscr L(X):=\left[\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}(R(g)-2\Lambda)-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}L_\varphi\right]\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If $X_1=X_0$ outside a compact set, its **relative total action** is
$S(X_1;X_0):=\mathcal I_M(\mathscr L(X_1)-\mathscr L(X_0))$. The scalar
and Maxwell relative actions are defined by their respective summands. No
subtraction of divergent global integrals is intended. When the separate
global integrals are defined and finite, this agrees with their difference.

Allowed independent directions are smooth compactly supported symmetric
inverse-metric tensors $q^{ab}$, real one-forms $\alpha$, and complex scalars
$\eta$. Near zero parameter use

$$g_\varepsilon^{-1}=g^{-1}+\varepsilon q,\qquad A_\varepsilon=A+\varepsilon\alpha,\qquad\varphi_\varepsilon=\varphi+\varepsilon\eta.$$

The parameter interval is restricted to preserve signature, time orientation,
and the potential domain. Stationarity means that the derivative of the
relative total action vanishes for every such direction. These definitions
include the original smooth trivial-potential system as a subclass, with its
same action coefficients and tensors. They do not change the separate
nontrivial-circle-bundle formulation or impose an integer condition on the
real coupling $\lambda$.

items.statement:
Use the classical finite-regularity configuration, relative actions and compact
smooth directions of
[[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]. In particular
the underlying manifold is smooth, $g\in C^3$, $A,\varphi\in C^2$,
$F=dA$, $P=\mathcal D\varphi$, and the constants and potential have exactly
that Definition's hypotheses. Then all compact first variations exist, and

$$\delta S=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\mathcal I_M\!\left(\left[G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab})\right]q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g\right)+\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\mathcal I_M\!\left((\nabla_aF^{ab}+\mu_0j^b)\alpha_b\mathrm{vol}_g\right)+\frac{K_\varphi}{c}\operatorname{Re}\mathcal I_M\!\left(\overline\eta E_\varphi\mathrm{vol}_g\right).$$

The scalar and free Maxwell summands separately have first variations

$$\delta S_\varphi=-\frac{1}{2c}\mathcal I_M(T^\varphi_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g)+\frac1c\mathcal I_M(j^a\alpha_a\mathrm{vol}_g)+\frac{K_\varphi}{c}\operatorname{Re}\mathcal I_M(\overline\eta E_\varphi\mathrm{vol}_g),$$

$$\delta S_{\mathrm{EM}}=-\frac{1}{2c}\mathcal I_M(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g)+\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\mathcal I_M((\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\mathrm{vol}_g).$$

Thus compact stationarity is equivalent to all the pointwise classical
charged-scalar equations in that Definition. The homogeneous equation
$dF=0$ holds identically in the global-potential domain.

Without assuming the Einstein, Maxwell or scalar field equations, one also
has the classical identities

$$\nabla_a j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi E_\varphi),\qquad \nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_\varphi}P_b)+F_{ba}j^a,$$

$$\nabla_a(T^{\mathrm{EM}})^a{}_b=\mu_0^{-1}F_{ba}\nabla_cF^{ca}.$$

Consequently the scalar equation implies current conservation, and the scalar
and sourced Maxwell equations together imply
$\nabla_a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi)^a{}_b=0$ before any Einstein equation
is used. These conclusions are valid for the stated classical fields with
continuous coefficients; they claim no lower roughness threshold, smoothing,
physical adoption or coupled-solution existence.

items.title: Temporal-gauge first-order reduction of the charged scalar equation
items.design_state: Complete conditional scalar principal-block calculation authored, including the compatibility substitution that removes mixed time derivatives. The actual charged-system and symmetric-hyperbolic-definition suppliers retain their current draft or pending-precheck statuses.
items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ be a coordinate region with $x^0=s$ a length coordinate, and let $g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $U$. Write $g^{ab}$ for its inverse and $\Gamma^c{}_{ab}$ for its Levi–Civita coefficients. Assume throughout the region that

$$g^{00}<0,\qquad (g^{ij})_{i,j=1}^3\text{ is positive definite}.$$

Let $A_0=0$, let $A_i$ be real, let $F_{0i}$ be real, and let $\varphi$ be complex. Treat $\pi_0,\pi_i$ as independent complex variables, and set

$$D_a\pi_b:=\partial_a\pi_b-\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\pi_c-i\lambda A_a\pi_b,$$

where $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $D_a\pi^a:=g^{ab}D_a\pi_b$. The temporal-gauge scalar first-order system is

$$\partial_s\varphi=\pi_0,\qquad \partial_sA_i=F_{0i},$$

$$\partial_s\pi_i-\partial_i\pi_0=-i\lambda A_i\pi_0-i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi,\qquad D_a\pi^a=V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi.$$

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in the periodic coefficient convention of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]. Use the three spatial compatibility equations to eliminate $\partial_s\pi_i$ from the scalar divergence equation. Then multiply the resulting scalar row by $-1$ and the compatibility rows by $g^{ki}$. For the variable block $(\pi_0,\pi_i)$, the resulting principal matrices are

$$A^0=\begin{pmatrix}-g^{00}&0\\0&g^{ij}\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^k=\begin{pmatrix}-2g^{0k}&-g^{kj}\\-g^{ik}&0\end{pmatrix}\quad(k=1,2,3).$$

The matrices on the complex variables mean the same real matrices on each real and imaginary component. They are symmetric and $A^0$ is positive definite. The transport equations for $\varphi$ and $A_i$ add only identity time blocks and no spatial derivative blocks. All remaining coefficients depend smoothly on $(g,g^{-1},\partial g,A,F,\varphi,\pi)$ wherever the stated metric inequalities and the open domain of $V$ hold. Thus this scalar-potential reduction is symmetric hyperbolic in the coefficient sense of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]].

items.title: Charged-scalar compatibility, Maxwell constraints and Einstein gauge propagation
items.design_state: Complete conditional metric, scalar, potential, sourced-Maxwell, stress-conservation and Einstein-gauge propagation authored. Batch-4, batch-6 and batch-7 drafts and imported GR suppliers retain their exact unresolved proof statuses.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the imported Sobolev and finite-domain integration results. Let $\Sigma=\{s=0\}$ be a spacelike slice in a smooth time-coordinate region $U\subset I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with future unit normal $n$ and induced metric $h$. Use the global-potential system of [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] in temporal gauge $A_0=0$, including $\partial_sA_i=F_{0i}$ and the scalar first-order equations of [[lem-emg-temporal-scalar-positive-symmetric-reduction]]. Treat $\pi_a$ and $F_{ab}$ as independent evolution variables. Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and $\mathcal D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$ for the charged derivatives of the model suppliers. In this item $D$ denotes only the spatial Levi-Civita derivative of $h$; thus $D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi$ on a scalar, while $\mathcal D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi-i\lambda A_i\varphi$.

Fix a smooth background metric $\bar g$ and define

$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc}\bigr)$$

as in [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Let $D$ be the Levi–Civita derivative of $h$, let $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, and put $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK$. Define the scalar and magnetic-potential residuals

$$C_i:=\pi_i-\partial_i\varphi+i\lambda A_i\varphi,\qquad B_{ij}:=F_{ij}-(\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i).$$

Assume the reduced scalar, sourced Maxwell, and harmonic-reduced Einstein evolution equations hold on $U$. The metric is in the admissible region of [[lem-emg-temporal-scalar-positive-symmetric-reduction]], with $g^{00}<0$ and positive definite $(g^{ij})$. The Maxwell field-strength evolution equations are the normal contractions $\iota_n(dF)=0$ and $\iota_n(d\star_gF-\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g)=0$, with the algebraic current source added to the Maxwell block. If $\partial_s=\alpha n+\beta^i\partial_i$, their coordinate-time contractions can contain shift multiples of the all-spatial residuals; no coordinate-time residual is set to zero before those spatial constraints are recovered. Assume initially

$$C_i=0,\qquad B_{ij}=0,\qquad D_i b^i=0,\qquad D_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad H|_\Sigma=0,$$

where in a positively oriented future orthonormal frame $F_{0i}=-e_i$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$, $\epsilon_{123}=1$, and $j^0=-n_aj^a$. Assume also the total-stress Einstein constraints

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\tau=\kappa T(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma),$$

where $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(X):=h^{ij}(D_{\partial_i}K)(\partial_j,X)$. The momentum constraint is an equality of covectors, independent of the choice of spatial coordinates or orthonormal frame.

For the metric first-order state $p_{ab}=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$, require their initial values to equal the corresponding metric derivatives.

Then on a neighborhood of every initial point:

1. $C_i=0$ and $B_{ij}=0$ persist, so $\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi$ and $F=dA$.
2. The scalar equation gives $\nabla_a j^a=0$, and the sourced Maxwell evolution together with the two initial Gauss constraints gives $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$.
3. Before Einstein-equation recovery, $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab})=0$.
4. The metric first-order derivative variables remain derivatives of the metric, and harmonic gauge propagates; hence the reduced Einstein equation is the full Einstein equation.

These statements hold for smooth solutions. They also hold for the classical finite-regularity system of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]], with $g\in C^3$, $A,\varphi\in C^2$ and the evolved $F,\pi\in C^2$ supplied at periodic Sobolev order $s\ge5$. Smooth underlying coordinates and background are retained; smoothness of the physical fields is not inferred.

items.title: Local classical Einstein–Maxwell–charged-scalar development
items.design_state: Complete conditional periodic and general smooth local-development proof authored. Its exact analytic, geometric and subsidiary suppliers remain at their inspected draft/pending-verification statuses.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice $\mathrm{DC}$ ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix an integer $s\ge5$, constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $K_\varphi>0$, $\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and a real $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U)$ on an open $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the attained values of $|\varphi|^2$. Use the system and units of [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] for smooth fields and its explicit classical extension [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]] for the finite-Sobolev branch.

Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and $\mathcal D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$ for the charged derivatives of the model suppliers. In this item $D$ denotes only the spatial Levi-Civita derivative of $h$; thus $D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi$ on a scalar, while $\mathcal D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi-i\lambda A_i\varphi$.

For any initial three-manifold $\Sigma$ with Riemannian metric $h$ below, use the abstract initial Lorentzian bundle $\mathcal V_\Sigma:=\mathbb R n\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $g_\Sigma(an+X,bn+Y):=-ab+h(X,Y)$ for $a,b\in\mathbb R$ and $X,Y\in T\Sigma$, as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]. Here $n$ is the distinguished future unit generator, realized as the future unit normal in any spacetime development; the data definition does not presuppose that development. For the periodic Cauchy result let $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and orient it by its ordered periodic coordinates, as in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Prescribe a real symmetric metric $h\in H^{s+1}$ whose continuous representative satisfies $h\ge c_0I$ for some $c_0>0$, a symmetric tensor $K\in H^s$, spatial vector fields $e,b\in H^s$, a global real spatial one-form $A_\Sigma\in H^s$, a complex scalar $\varphi_0\in H^{s+1}$, and an independent complex datum $\pi_n\in H^s$ for the normal component of the charged derivative, realized by $\mathcal D_n\varphi|_\Sigma=\pi_n$. All Sobolev spaces are real componentwise spaces with complex fields split into real and imaginary parts, as in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Let $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ be any positively oriented $h$-orthonormal spatial frame. The associated initial two-form $F_\Sigma$ on $\mathcal V_\Sigma$ is defined invariantly by

$$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X),\qquad F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)\quad(X,Y\in T\Sigma).$$

Thus, writing $e_i=h(e,\mathfrak e_i)$ and $b_i=h(b,\mathfrak e_i)$, its frame components are $F_\Sigma(\mathfrak e_i,n)=e_i$ and $F_\Sigma(\mathfrak e_i,\mathfrak e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$, with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$. Require $F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$, $\pi_i=(\mathcal D_i\varphi_0)=\partial_i\varphi_0-i\lambda A_{\Sigma,i}\varphi_0$, and $A(n)=0$. Fix a smooth positive reference metric $\gamma$ and the product comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\gamma$ near the initial slice. The harmonic-gauge vector is $H^a:=g^{bc}(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc})$; prescribe the following initial metric jet relative to this fixed smooth background:

$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\quad g_{00}=-1,\quad g_{0i}=0,\quad \partial_0g_{ij}=2K_{ij},\quad \partial_0g_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK,\quad \partial_0g_{0i}=h_{ij}h^{k\ell}(\Gamma(h)^j{}_{k\ell}-\Gamma(\gamma)^j{}_{k\ell}).$$

Let $D$ be the Levi–Civita derivative of $h$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK$, and $T=T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi$ be evaluated on the complete initial data. Define $j^0:=-n_aj^a$ in the normal frame and assume the sourced Maxwell and total-stress Einstein constraints

$$D_i b^i=0,\qquad D_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\tau=\kappa T(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma),$$

where $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)=h^{ij}(D_{\partial_i}K)(\partial_j,X)$, $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$, and $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ in a spacetime realization. The constraint expressions are interpreted using their continuous representatives at the stated Sobolev orders. On the reduced coordinate domain require $g^{00}<0$ and the inverse spatial block $(g^{ij})$ to be positive definite. The real first-order state consists of the metric variables $(g_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi})$ relative to a fixed smooth background, the six Maxwell variables $(e_i,b_i)$, the three potential components $A_i$, and the real and imaginary parts of $\varphi,\pi_0,\pi_i$. For fixed reference scales $L_0>0$ metres and $F_0>0$ tesla, replace each first metric derivative $v$ and each $\pi_a$ by $L_0v$ and $L_0\pi_a$, each $e_i,b_i$ by $e_i/F_0,b_i/F_0$, and each $A_i$ by $A_i/(L_0F_0)$; $g_{ab}$ and $\varphi$ are already dimensionless. These fixed invertible rescalings make the componentwise real Sobolev state dimensionless and add no equations. Let $u_0$ be the resulting state in the sense of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], and suppose its continuous range is a compact $K_0$ contained in the interior of a compact $K_1$ inside an open admissible state set $O$, with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ and $R\ge0$. On an open time interval $I\ni0$, the complete periodic coefficient maps are smooth jointly on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ as in [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]; the potential range lies in $\mathcal U$, and the combined time matrix is positive definite throughout $O$.

Then there is $T_*>0$ and a local solution on $(-T_*,T_*)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ of the full Einstein, sourced Maxwell, and classical charged-scalar equations. Its first-order metric and matter state has the $L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ regularity of [[thm-emg-symmetric-hyperbolic-research-supplier]]; the metric satisfies $g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$ and $\partial_0g\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$, while $F,\pi,A_i\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$. The constraints and first-order metric, scalar, and potential compatibility conditions propagate. Smooth data give a smooth development on the same local interval.

More generally, let $\Sigma$ be any smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary. Prescribe a smooth positive-definite metric $h\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*\Sigma)$, a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $K\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*\Sigma)$, smooth spatial vector fields $e,b\in C^\infty(\Sigma;T\Sigma)$, a smooth global one-form $A_\Sigma\in C^\infty(\Sigma;T^*\Sigma)$, a complex scalar $\varphi_0\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\mathbb C)$, and an independent complex datum $\pi_n\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\mathbb C)$ realized by $\mathcal D_n\varphi|_\Sigma=\pi_n$ on $\mathcal V_\Sigma$. Define $F_\Sigma$ on $\mathcal V_\Sigma$ by the same $h,e,b$ convention in local positively oriented orthonormal frames, without requiring a global frame. Require $F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$, $\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi_0$, $A(n)=0$, and the sourced Maxwell and total-stress Einstein constraints displayed above at every point of $\Sigma$. Restrict to neighborhoods where $|\varphi|^2\in\mathcal U$. Then the data have a smooth local development near each initial point. Any two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the initial surface by a data-fixing, time-orientation-preserving isometry and a global-potential gauge transformation

$$A\mapsto A+d\chi,\qquad \varphi\mapsto e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi,$$

for a smooth real $\chi$ with $\chi=0$ on the initial surface; under the formal units of [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]], $[\chi]=\mathrm{Wb}$ so $\lambda\chi$ is dimensionless. No nontrivial bundle sector, singular source, global-in-time existence, uniform noncompact time width, or geodesic completeness is asserted.

title: Trivial-potential classical charged scalar system — Examples

items.title: Zero scalar with V(0)=0 reduces to electrovacuum
items.design_state: The zero-field reduction and exact-potential converse are proved directly; the local-existence instance is conditional on the assigned development theorem.
items.statement: Use [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] and suppose $0\in\mathcal U$ and $V(0)=0$. Let $\varphi\equiv0$ and $\pi_a\equiv0$. Then the scalar equation, current, and scalar stress vanish, and the full coupled field equations reduce exactly to the source-free Einstein–Maxwell equations. Conversely, any smooth source-free Einstein–Maxwell solution on this region that admits the global potential $F=dA$ is a solution of the defined charged-scalar system with $\varphi=0$. The condition $V(0)=0$ is essential for the zero scalar stress conclusion. In particular, source-free initial data in this exact-potential sector that satisfy the local-development theorem's hypotheses have a smooth local realization in this branch.

items.title: Classical scalar sector and bundle limitation
items.design_state: The remark records the exact global-potential limitation stated by the assigned definition.
items.statement: [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] uses a globally defined real one-form $A$ and $F=dA$, so it describes only the trivial-potential sector. It does not cover a connection on an arbitrary nontrivial principal $U(1)$ bundle, a scalar represented only by local sections with nontrivial transition functions, or singular currents. In this global real-potential sector $\lambda$ may be any real number; charge quantization belongs to a separately specified bundle representation and is not inferred here. The field $\varphi$ is a classical complex field, not a quantum amplitude, and no value of $\hbar$ is used.
